name: Landing page
summary: A single-page argument: one promise, proof, three reasons, how it works, price, objections, one repeated call to action.
principles: One primary call to action, repeated at the end; every other link is secondary.
Above the fold: what it is, who it is for, the primary action, nothing else competing.
Each section answers one question a visitor has, in the order they have it.
Generous vertical rhythm between sections (the direction's largest spacing steps); tighter rhythm inside them.
Real, specific copy. A headline someone could disagree with beats one nobody remembers.
structure_note: Single column of full-width sections with a constrained content width (about 64-72rem). Alternate nothing for decoration's sake: separate sections with space and a hairline, not background stripes or gradients.

sections.name: Navigation
sections.purpose: Orient and offer the primary action without stealing attention from the hero.
guidance: Logo or wordmark left, 2 to 4 text links, one primary button right.
No mega menus on a landing page. Collapse links into a menu below about 40rem width.
Sticky only if the page is long; keep it the bg color with a bottom hairline.

platform_notes.web: Use <header> and <nav aria-label="Main">; the theme toggle is an icon button with aria-label.

sections.name: Hero
sections.purpose: Say what it is, who it is for and what to do next in five seconds.
guidance: Eyebrow (label role) naming the audience, headline (display role), one or two sentence subline (body, muted).
Primary button plus at most one secondary action. Never two primaries.
Left-aligned text reads faster than centered for anything longer than one line.
A product screenshot or real photograph beats abstract 3D shapes or gradient blobs.

copy.notes: State the outcome, not the feature. No 'Welcome to the future of X', no 'Unlock your potential'.

sections.name: Social proof
sections.purpose: Show that real people or companies already trust it.
guidance: A row of customer names or logos in muted text, or one short quote with a name and role, or one hard number.
Monochrome logos only; colored logos fight the accent.
Never fake: no invented logos, no 'Trusted by 10,000+ teams' without a source.

sections.name: Three reasons
sections.purpose: Give the three strongest reasons to choose it.
guidance: Three blocks maximum, in a row on desktop, stacked on mobile.
Each: short title (title role) and one or two sentences (body-small, muted). An icon is optional and must come from one set.
Cards use surface + hairline border; no shadows, no glow, no gradient icons.

sections.name: How it works
sections.purpose: Remove uncertainty about effort: three numbered steps.
guidance: Numbered steps (01, 02, 03 in tabular label style), each with a title and one sentence.
Show the real product at the step where it matters most.

sections.name: Pricing
sections.purpose: Make the price and what it includes unambiguous.
guidance: Two or three plans. Highlight the recommended one with an accent border, not a gradient or a scale transform.
Prices in tabular numerals; the period ('per month') in muted body text.
Each plan states who it is for in one line and has its own action.

sections.name: FAQ
sections.purpose: Answer the objections that stop people from acting.
guidance: Five to eight real questions as native disclosure elements (details/summary) or accessible accordions.
Answers are direct and specific: security, cancellation, data, pricing changes.

sections.name: Final call to action
sections.purpose: Repeat the single primary action once the case has been made.
guidance: Restate the outcome in one line (headline role) and repeat the same primary button label as the hero.
No new information and no new offers here.

sections.name: Footer
guidance: Muted body-small text, grouped links, legal line, no marketing copy.
Contact and status links where relevant (support, security, status page).

states.name: No JavaScript
states.guidance: Content and links work without scripts; the theme falls back to the system setting.

states.name: Form error
states.guidance: If the hero or final CTA has an email field, show inline errors in the error color with text, not color alone.

states.name: Success
states.guidance: After sign-up, confirm in place with what happens next (for example 'Check your inbox').

accessibility: One h1 (the hero headline); sections use h2 in order.
Every image has alt text or alt="" when decorative.
Visible focus styles on every link and button; a skip link to main content.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion for any scroll or entrance animation.
avoid: Gradient hero backgrounds, floating blobs, glassmorphism cards
More than three feature blocks or a features grid of nine
Stock photos of people pointing at laptops
